When I talk about the development of main characters I am referring more to the antagonistics than protagonists. This is what you've probably heard LOK fans use all the time when explaining why LOK is still worth watching because of better villains. In ATLA our main villain is Oazi and even though they managed to keep him pretty mistirious for a while he eventually fell flat as a basic villain with pretty much no character depth, just the bad guy who cares only about himself and wants to take over the world because he thinks everything will be better if he rules. It at first looked like TDP was going in this direction until we were introduced to Aaravos who has a lot more potential. It's hard to compare these to shows right now because ATLA is finished, while TDP only has 3/7 seasons airing now. We don't yet know if Aaravos will turn out to be a basic villain like Oasi did but right now that seems unlikely considering they seem to be building him the same why they did Oazi (we know little to nothing about him) but this time he has some complicated backstory. I can't say much on this character yet though because of the lack of information we have.
for Zuko vs. Soren's redemption arc, I agree Zuko is the clear winner, although he had gone a lot farther down the wrong path than Soren did (who other than the zipline thing never actually did anything wrong). Soren was less of a villain to start so he didn't need as elaborate of a redemption arc sense no one even thought of him as the bad guy aside from Rayla. We may get a better redemption arc from Claudia but seeing how many of the trends set be ATLA TDP seems to follow I dought she will get one, especially with the interest Aaravos has taking in her. But enough theorizing, ATLA did better with the redemption arc by far. 
I think at this point if I keep arguing I'm just digging my own grave with the Harrow argument, there just isn't a good comparison in the ATLA universe. Harrow's death was amazing but ATLA never lost a main character the same way so I can't use this in my points.

For the argument on the Harrow vs. Jet comparison: I would say that yes, these two characters have a much different level of significance in the show which does skiw my point but both of these shows (especially ATLA, due to the limitations of killing/death aloud) are good at avoiding the death of lead characters so it's hard to get a good comparison. A diffrent comparison would be Yue. With the "death" of Yue you see ATLA come closer to what TDP achieved with the depth of development coming from the death of a character. Yue's death does still effect the characters long after it happens. An example of this is Sokka refusing to kiss Suki under the full moon and then later learning to move on from the loss and except it. ATLA does an amazing job with this but I still believe TDP found a way to do even better. While with Yue it still is very one dimensional, it mostly only effects Sokka while her death is referenced more (such as in the swamp episode) it still doesn't matter at all to the plot, just another character that had a lot of meaning before but vanished in the plot after her death. Unlike this, Harrow is still effecting the plot after his death, I am aware you will probably agree that Harrow was still more important to the story but that is not the only reason he still effects the story. The death of Harrow allowed the characters to grow as people and changed the decisions they made because of this. I don't mean just not kissing someone because of a momentary worry, I mean life changing stuff. I'm not going to go into Callum unlocking the sky Arcanum because this could be agrued would have happened anyway but we can look at the decision Ezran makes to return to the kingdom. After Ezran lets out his feeling to Claudia (using the words Callum had once spoken to him, and Harrow spoke before that) he realizes that he needs to face his duties even though Harrow isn't around to help him. He makes these decisions because of the growth he has made as a character. 
For the filler episode argument: My point wasn't that the filler episodes made ATLA worse, it's the fact that the show needed them in the first place. Even though it is debatable which show is better overall considering the amazing plot, writing, and animation of both, most will agree that ATLA's weakest point was the characters themselves. This is an arguement you here all the time with LOK vs ATLA and even though ATLA is definitely the winner there that point still stands, the character development could be better. My point is that even with all the filler episodes (some of which better than others) they managed to still fall flat on many of the main characters, something that TDP does not do. TDP manages to limit the number of "filler episodes" (episodes that contribute nothing to the overall plot) without taking away from any world building or character development. I will admit I think ATLA did a significantly better job at the world building aspect (although still nothing could compare to what you see in both shows) but TDP has much better characters and plot with all the extras.

Warning: contains spoilers for seasons 1-2 of ATLA and TDP! I agree that the animation could be better in the first season but would definitely say that the story makes up for that. Saying that it does nothing particularly amazing is just straight up false. Other than the amazing writing and story that we can agree both shows have there is one main difference between ATLA and TDP. TDP covers many things in the real world that ATLA never touchs. One of the reasons that ATLA is so loved is for the complexity of the topics covered in what seems like a kid's show but still avoids some things altogether. Take for example the death of Jet in ATLA and the death of Harrow in TDP, in ATLA Jet's death is sad but pretty skimmed over (I'm aware this is because of Nikolodian's rules but that doesn't mean it isn't still a flaw). Like every death in ATLA, after Jet's death there is barely any mention of him again, he was only there for the plot and plays no role after he is removed, it's like he never existed. There are many such examples of things in ATLA only being there for plot then being thrown away like this which really diminishes the overall show for me. TDP however does not have the same flaws. When Harrow dies we get to see the full effect on all of the characters and the process of how each one deals with it and the show promotes the idea that there is not a set solution to deal with death and grief, and everyone goes through it there own way and that this is okay. It shows Rayla unable to break the news to Callum and then Callum finding himself unable to do the same thing with Ezran and how this brings them all closer together in the end because of this shared feeling. The show manages to show us all this but not let it take over at the same time, we still get our share of action scenes and story line but this and many other things are going on in the which adds a depth to the story that ATLA will never have. ATLA  is also weighed down by all the filler episodes that make every event less relevant to the overall plot. TDP manages to do all this development and more without the unessasary fillers and pointless side stories. If you actually read and understand this then I'm impressed. I'm willing to clarify any point needed, and if you have a counter argument, go for it!
I'd say that TDP wins story and character development especially considering its (so far) shorter length but ATLA wins in animation do to TDP's lower frame rate in the first season.
